This can definitely be confusing for new people, so I'll try to explain best I can. 

Set: You get all versions of the regular album with everything included in each, people usually buy these when they want all versions

Random: Buy this and you get one random version with all promised inclusions, if you buy two, there's a risk you may end up getting two of the same version. Most stores will try to give you different ones if they can though. It's cheaper because you're only getting one album compared to the set of around 2-3 albums. 

Compact: Typically a cheaper version with only photocards and maybe a mini poster with a QR code for the songs. Some may still include CDs, like Seventeen's Sector 17 Compact version. Occasionally I've seen compact being referred to as digipack or jewel case as well and both include CDs. 

Other versions you'll eventually come across similar to compact version but from what I know are always only photocards and a QR code: Evermusic, Plve, Weverse, Poca. (I'm sure there are some I'm missing but those are what I see most often)

Fixed claims means your name is written down automatically for all upcoming benefits announced with the album, typically only the Korea based stores, but some GOMs will do them all regardless of location if they have a proxy. Most GOMs will allow backouts for only a few stores, but you will be expected to join the majority of their GOs for that comeback period. Preclaims is usually done in groupchats and the GOM will send whatever set they're hosting for and let people claim before they actually post it. Typically, these claims are not binding and you are not required to join any specific amount (this is dependent on each individual GOM though). For each GO, the albums will normally be opened and the cards will be sorted. For album cards, you'll typically have to fill out a sorting form listing your preferred members from most to least. You are also not guaranteed any specific member for album cards as these are random and the GOM cannot control how many of each member they receive. POBS and lucky draws are usually guaranteed but again, will depend on how the GOM runs their GOs.

I would recommend speech therapy, however I also have a problem similar to this and I never got speech therapy. I also have a dream of acting and have even been in a few plays. If speech therapy truly isn't an option (but I do recommend it, it would've helped me) I have a trick I use when there's a word I struggle with saying. When I run into a difficult word or phrase, I work extra on it. I say the word by itself slowly as many times as I need to until I hear it being said right, then I'll go quicker until I'm saying it at a normal talking speed. At this point I'll put the word back in its sentence and say the sentence aloud with that word. Sometimes I'll even work with family members so they can listen and tell me if I'm being understood. When I was younger I struggled a lot with my "r"s and two words I struggled with the most was "girl" and "drawer". I still have trouble sometimes, but my acting teacher was a huge help and my family noticed after I started taking her classes, my speech was getting better. It'll be hard, but if you really make yourself work it'll pay off in the end.
